findings.summary: Stripping all HTML tags from placeholder detection hides genuine token remnants inside visible alt text or malformed tags, while concatenating removed tags can hide adjacent boundary-sensitive fragments.
findings.recommendation: Separate provider-response token validation from cached visible-content filtering. In provider residual text, reject token remnants without stripping markup/URLs. In cache filtering, preserve whitespace at stripped boundaries and inspect alt text while excluding supplier URL values.

findings.summary: A provider can add literal HTML outside protected tokens and still pass counts/order; restored HTML is then no longer the protected source structure.
findings.recommendation: Reject raw HTML tokens left outside expected protected tokens, or compare exact restored HTML token sequence to the pre-protection source token sequence before cache write.

findings.summary: Old cache values lacking protected HTML are returned without structural validation because no placeholder remains. This predates the diff; new fresh-result guard does not repair historic cache corruption.
findings.recommendation: Either validate cached source-to-value protected structure or explicitly version/invalidate old cache entries in a separate migration.

passingAreas: Missing, duplicated, mangled and reordered expected HTML tokens rejected.
Glossary token reordering with same multiplicities allowed.
Entire HTTP batch token restoration validated before first successful cache write; second-item failure sends both to fallback without poisoning first item.
Supplier URL fragments can be excluded without blocking clean cache entries.
